The title held by the first governor‑general of India was simply **“Governor‑General of India.”**  
William Cavendish‑Bentinck was the inaugural holder of that office, serving from 22 April 1834 to 20 March 1835, when it was established as the head of the British administration over the entire territory controlled by the East India Company (later the Crown) [1].  

**Position:** Governor‑General of India (the British crown’s chief representative and head of the colonial government in India).  

---

**Source**

[1] *Lord William Bentinck* – “...he served as the first governor-general of India from 1828 to 1835,” with an infobox indicating his tenure as *Governor‑General of India* 22 April 1834 – 20 March 1835. (Wikipedia, 2004‑04‑22)
